_comment: Copy to ~/.config/quickshell/notifications.json to change notification placement,
motion or timing. The live shell re-reads it on save — no restart, no QML edit.
Every key is optional; anything missing or invalid falls back to the shipped default
in config/NotifyConfig.qml. Delete the file to go back to defaults.
preset: right-center (default) | bottom-center | top-right.
The placement block below overrides individual preset values.
QS_NOTIFY_PRESET in the environment wins over this file.
anchorH: left | center | right      anchorV: top | center | bottom
stack:   down (newest nearest the top) | up (newest nearest the bottom)
screenName: monitor name to pin popups to; empty = whichever monitor has focus.
Per-source pinning is a rules-engine job (Notifications.rulesHook).
entrance: slide | scale | fade | none
exit:     dwell (fly into the bar bell) | slide | fade | none
timing:   ms per urgency. >0 = show that long, 0 = sticky (stays until dismissed),
-1 = drawer-only: recorded and counted unread, never popped.
respectAppTimeout honours the client's own expire_timeout request.
hoverPause: the pointer over a card freezes its countdown; showRemaining draws it.
burstAt/burstMs: once a stack holds burstAt cards (0 = placement.maxVisible), further
non-critical cards are capped at burstMs so the stack drains. burstMs 0 = off.
criticalCollapseMs: a sticky card folds to an icon pill this long after it appears;
one click expands it again. 0 = never collapse.
rules:  Lua rules engine. path empty = ~/.config/quickshell/notifications.lua
(QS_NOTIFY_RULES overrides). timeoutMs is the fail-open budget: past it the
notification is shown with its defaults and the interpreter is restarted.
See notifications.example.lua. A rule can never drop a notification.
surface: opacity of the popup cards and the docked pills. Cards stay mostly solid —
one lands over whatever you are working in and has to be readable at a glance.
collapse: where a folded sticky card goes. home "bar" docks it as a floating pill in
the bar between the workspaces and the status cluster (no bar background of its
own); "stack" leaves it in the popup stack. maxPills caps the tray, then one
"+N" chip opens the drawer. Click a pill to unfold it back into a popup.
drawer.opacity / itemOpacity: the slab is glass (and blurred by the compositor via the
layer rule in hypr/lua/windowrules.lua) while the ROWS stay opaque — background is
atmosphere, notifications are content.
drawer: history UI. mode panel = full-height slab on the right edge, modal = centred
launcher-shaped dialog; same rows and same keys either way. limit is how many
stored rows one page pulls. Clearing from the drawer never deletes a row.
store:  SQLite history at ${XDG_DATA_HOME:-~/.local/share}/quickshell/notifications.db
(QS_NOTIFY_DB overrides the path). Retention is age AND count, whichever bites
first; 0 on either turns that limit off. Query it from anywhere, no shell needed:
sqlite3 -readonly ~/.local/share/quickshell/notifications.db \
"SELECT received_at, app_name, summary FROM notifications ORDER BY received_at DESC LIMIT 20;"

prompt._comment: A prompt is offered on a client inline-reply hint, on one of these categories, or when a matching action declares `prompt`. The list is written down rather than left to taste: a prompt belongs where a text reply is the notification's natural response AND the reply has somewhere to go. 'Build failed' gets actions, not a prompt.

snooze._comment: `s` in focus mode snoozes for defaultMs; `r` prompts for a delay (20m, 2h, 90s, 17:30). maxMs bounds a parsed value rather than trusting it. A snooze is a row in the history store, so it survives a qs restart and a reboot. presets are extra one-click chips beyond the default-duration one, each a duration string parsed the same way — keep the list short, this is a snooze row on every card, not a duration picker.

timers._comment: Timers, pomodoro, stopwatch and alarms (`qs ipc call timers …`). Lengths and the cycle count are config because a pomodoro is a personal rhythm. addMs is what the card's "+N min" action adds. anchorV is why a running timer does not fight the notification stack: the overlay draws one window per (monitor, anchor) pair, so pinning timers to the top gives them their own stack — set either anchor to "" to follow `placement`. stopwatchPill = false hides the bar readout.

actions._comment: AGENT / CI. Matcher keys: app, category, urgency, summary, body, hint.<name>. A `~` prefix is a regex, anything else is exact and case-insensitive. `run` is argv — {id} {app} {summary} {body} {input} {hint:NAME} are substituted as ELEMENTS, never spliced into a shell string, so a summary containing `; rm -rf` is an argument.
actions.label: Attach

actions._comment: HOMELAB. Opening a runbook or dashboard is the common case; ack goes through whatever CLI the alerting stack provides.
actions.label: Runbook

actions._comment: VAULT. Capture into Inbox/ with the notification as the body. A prompt turns it into 'capture with a note' — {input} is what you typed.
actions.label: Capture
